data.title: Week's Best: JPMorgan Chase Teams Overseeing $18 Billion Go Indie — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kenneth Corbin

Two financial advisor teams that managed $18.6 billion with JPMorgan Chase's wealth management division have left the company to launch an independent practice in one of the largest recent breakaway moves. Phil Scott and Jim Atwood are combining their practices to form a 41-person team they are calling Latigo Peak Partners, based in Palm Beach Gardens, Fla. The team leaders say they launched their own firm to have more flexibility and control over their business, which they say serves some of the most sophisticated families, entrepreneurs, and business owners in the country.

Among other most-read wealth management articles this week:

Capital Group and the great drawdown puzzle. Many financial advisors, to say nothing of their clients, struggle to calculate an appropriate schedule for converting a life's savings into retirement income. Capital Group, the largest provider of actively managed target-date funds, is trying to help with two new model approaches that offer suggested ranges for annual drawdowns of investors' retirement savings. One points toward a consistent income stream that could be a good fit for retirees trying to meet fixed expenses such as housing and healthcare, while the other is geared for people with more spending flexibility who might be concerned with achieving a legacy goal.

IRS cautions on 351 conversions. Investors and their advisors seeking to defer tax liability for capital gains have long leaned on a provision in the tax code that permits transfers of appreciated assets into exchange-traded funds, known as 351 exchanges. However, the IRS is signaling that it plans to take a closer look at those transactions, indicating that it might scrutinize moves that it sees as a pass-through conversion, trading one portfolio for another simply for tax purposes. The IRS recently published a call for comments from the public in an effort to gather information about how 351 exchanges are used in practice, which could potentially inform new rules on the issue.

Star Vanguard subadvisors debut new fund. How many investors know that since its launch in 1984, the Vanguard Primecap fund has been outperforming Vanguard's stalwart S&P index fund? Primecap is a longtime Vanguard subadvisor and institutional stock manager based in California that Vanguard founder Jack Bogle implored to launch a fund under the Vanguard umbrella. Now, more than 40 years later, Primecap is launching a new fund, the Primecap Odyssey Discovery, which is its first exchange-traded fund and exists outside the orbit of Vanguard's own funds. It will focus on small and midsize companies.

Could UBS become a Swiss expat? UBS, Switzerland's largest bank, holds a rarefied position in that country's economy, but it isn't crazy to imagine the lender pickup up stakes and leaving Zurich behind. That is because of the prospect of Switzerland implementing strict new capital requirements that could make UBS less competitive with its peers based in other nations. UBS declined to comment on the prospect of a move, and company executives have publicly said they would like to stay in Switzerland, but some investors are calling on the bank to relocate to a friendlier regulatory environment.

Weigh cash needs when sorting a portfolio. It's common for ultrawealthy families to organize their portfolios by asset class. That approach might make some sense, but our guest columnist, a veteran family office manager, argues that it ignores important liquidity questions that become important once the family needs cash. Our columnist offers a four-bucket system for ranking assets by liquidity: cash and near cash, including Bitcoin; the liquid middle, including public securities; the illiquid middle, including investments like private equity with lockup periods; and aspirational, referring to concentrated and illiquid investments, such as a family business.

Write to advisor.editors@barrons.com

data.title: Nvidia Sets Out Framework For Enterprise AI Agent Governance
data.description:
The framework combines infrastructure, monitoring and security controls to support AI agent deployment across enterprise and edge environments

Nvidia has outlined its OpenShell Reference Architecture at GTC Berlin for building, monitoring and governing artificial intelligence (AI) agents across enterprise and edge environments. The architecture brings together computing infrastructure and security tools intended to help organisations monitor agent behaviour and enforce operational policies.

The framework integrates Nvidia Vera Rubin infrastructure, Vera central processing units (CPUs) and BlueField-4 data processing units (DPUs) running Nvidia Sentry. According to the company’s description, the setup is designed to support agent-based workloads while enabling security policies to be enforced and agent behaviour to be monitored independently.

Technology Partners Involved

The initiative involves technology companies including Anthropic, AWS, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Dell Technologies, Google Cloud, HPE, IBM, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, SAP and ServiceNow.

The companies operate across areas such as cloud computing, enterprise software, cybersecurity and AI development. Their involvement brings together different technology providers around infrastructure and controls for deploying AI agents in business settings.

Focus On Monitoring And Controls

As businesses explore AI agents for tasks across different functions, managing their actions and access to systems has become an operational consideration. The architecture addresses this by combining infrastructure for running AI workloads with mechanisms for monitoring behaviour and enforcing defined security policies.

Nvidia has identified manufacturing, healthcare, retail, robotics and telecommunications as potential application areas. The framework is intended for enterprise and edge environments, where organisations may need to manage AI agents across different systems and operational settings.

Integrations With Enterprise Platforms

The architecture also includes integrations with SAP Joule Studio and ServiceNow Arc. These connect enterprise AI tools with governance, monitoring and security capabilities.

The development comes as businesses assess how to deploy AI agents while maintaining oversight of their activities. Beyond the capabilities of individual AI systems, implementation requires organisations to define access permissions, monitor agent actions and establish controls around the tasks they can perform.

Nvidia’s architecture brings these requirements together within a common framework, although the practical implications for businesses will depend on how the components are implemented and integrated into existing systems.

data.title: Infosys Q2 Profit Rises 6.2%, FY27 Revenue Growth Guidance Cut
data.description:
Infosys cut its FY27 revenue growth forecast to 1-2 per cent as weak North American demand and pressure in retail and high-tech offset strong deal wins worth $5.2 billion in the September quarter

Infosys cut its annual revenue growth forecast on Friday after reporting a 6.2 per cent rise in second-quarter net profit.

The company lowered its revenue growth guidance for the financial year ending March 2027 to 1-2 per cent in constant currency terms, from its previous forecast of 1.5-3 per cent, a more cautious outlook for the remainder of the year.

Consolidated net profit rose to Rs 7,823 crore in the July-September quarter from Rs 7,364 crore a year earlier.

Revenue increased 10.7 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to Rs 49,244 crore, marginally above market expectations of Rs 49,132 crore. In constant currency terms, which exclude the impact of exchange-rate movements, revenue grew 1.5 per cent from a year earlier and 1.2 per cent sequentially.

The Bengaluru-based company retained its operating margin forecast of 20-22 per cent for fiscal 2027, despite the weaker revenue outlook. Its operating margin stood at 21 per cent in the quarter, unchanged from a year earlier.

“We had strong large deals of USD 5.2 billion, including a mega deal of over USD 2 billion, reinforcing our position as a trusted partner in the marketplace when clients embark on large and complex transformation programs. Our AI revenue was at 10.5 per cent and grew 29 per cent quarter-on-quarter. As enterprises move to AI adoption at scale, the strong growth in AI revenues is a recognition of our differentiated market positioning and client confidence,” said Salil Parekh, CEO and MD at Infosys.

“We are advising some of the largest global enterprise on their AI strategy and continue to invest in deep domain and technology capabilities to bring new ideas and an integrated ecosystem to help businesses unlock AI value at scale,” he added.

The guidance reduction comes as India’s technology services industry navigates an uncertain spending environment, with clients scrutinising technology budgets and seeking productivity gains from artificial intelligence. AI-led automation is also changing traditional outsourcing models, as customers increasingly expect technology providers to deliver more work with fewer billable hours.

Deal Wins Strengthen

Infosys posted large deal wins with a total contract value of USD 5.2 billion during the quarter, up from USD 3.1 billion in the year-ago period. About 62 per cent of the wins were classified as net new business, indicating that a majority involved new contracts rather than renewals or extensions.

However, the strong deal pipeline has yet to translate into a comparable acceleration in reported revenue growth, leaving the pace of contract conversion a key factor for investors to monitor.

Performance across business segments remained uneven. Revenue from energy and utilities grew 7.3 per cent YoY in constant currency terms, while financial services expanded 2.1 per cent. Life sciences recorded growth of 32.5 per cent.

Retail revenue declined 7.7 per cent, while high-technology revenue fell 17.3 per cent, pointing to continued pressure in two segments that together account for a meaningful share of the company’s business.

Geographically, North America, which contributed 54.6 per cent of revenue, contracted 1.5 per cent in constant currency terms. Europe grew 4.6 per cent, while revenue from the rest of the world increased 10.9 per cent. India revenue declined 3.5 per cent.

The weakness in North America is particularly important because of the region’s large contribution to overall revenue. A sustained recovery in the market will be central to Infosys’ ability to improve growth in the coming quarters.

AI Revenue And Margins In Focus

Infosys said artificial intelligence accounted for 10.5 per cent of revenue and that AI revenue grew 29 per cent sequentially. The figures indicate rising demand for AI-related services, although the extent to which these revenues represent additional business rather than the transformation of existing technology contracts remains an important question for the sector.

Operating profit rose 10.4 per cent YoY to Rs 10,330 crore. However, total operating expenses increased 14.6 per cent to Rs 4,971 crore, outpacing revenue growth and adding to the challenge of sustaining margins as demand remains subdued.

“We delivered operating margins of 21.0 per cent in Q2 amidst heightened volatility. Focus on cost and operational efficiency measures while making the required investments, have led to stable margins,” said Jayesh Sanghrajka, CFO at Infosys.

Free cash flow stood at Rs 8,898 crore, down 8.1 per cent year-on-year, while cash and investments totalled Rs 45,232 crore at the end of September.

The company declared an interim dividend of Rs 26 per share, compared with Rs 23 per share a year earlier. The record date is November 3, with payment scheduled for November 11.

data.title: SBI Data Leak Puts Focus On Banks’ Expanding Cyber Risk
data.description:
Preliminary checks identified 3,897 customer records containing personal information among 375,000 records examined on the dark web, prompting calls for continuous security testing and tighter controls across banking systems and third-party networks

State Bank of India (SBI) is investigating a suspected customer data exposure after alerts received on 16 October led to the identification of 3,897 records containing personally identifiable information among approximately 375,000 records found on the dark web.

The lender has engaged an independent cybersecurity agency empanelled by the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) to determine the source, extent and potential impact of the exposure.

The incident puts the security of customer information under scrutiny as banks expand digital services and depend on interconnected applications, application programming interfaces (APIs) and external technology providers. While SBI has reported no material impact on its core operations or financial performance, the investigation has yet to establish how the data was exposed and whether the information was accessed through a breach of the bank's systems or another source.

Personal Data Exposure Raises Targeted Fraud Risks

The information identified in the preliminary review reportedly includes customers’ names, gender, registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, email and residential addresses, branch details, Customer Information File (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs and metadata associated with loan and lead records. SBI has not established the complete extent or authenticity of the data, and the findings do not by themselves establish that customer accounts were accessed or funds stolen.

Shikhil Sharma, founder and chief executive of Astra Security, said application-level weaknesses often emerge at the points where banking systems connect, including APIs, mobile applications and third-party integrations. He said vulnerabilities could arise when individual components were tested separately but weaknesses in the overall customer journey remained undetected.

“The real risk is rarely a single bug. It is a chain, where attackers combine two or three minor flaws to walk through an entire banking workflow,” Sharma said, recommending that banks test complete customer journeys, including login, payments and beneficiary changes.

The distinction is important for banks that rely on multiple digital systems to deliver a single customer-facing service. Security reviews that focus on individual applications may not identify weaknesses involving permissions, authentication or the exchange of information between connected systems.

Periodic Security Audits Face Pressure To Evolve

Manish Chasta, co-founder and chief technology officer of Eventus Security, said the expanding relationships between banking applications, payment systems, infrastructure providers and external services had widened the potential attack surface. Weak APIs, excessive permissions, compromised service accounts and inadequate network segmentation could allow an attacker to move from an initial point of access to more sensitive systems.

Chasta said banks needed continuous attack-surface management, identity threat detection, API security testing and stronger network segmentation. He also called for better integration of security logs across applications, identities and networks to help banks identify suspicious activity and determine the extent of a compromise more quickly.

Sharma said periodic penetration testing remained valuable but could not, on its own, keep pace with systems that change through frequent software releases and new integrations. He recommended combining continuous automated testing with experienced human testers who can identify business-logic and access-control flaws that automated tools may miss. The approach would allow banks to test new releases and integrations as they are introduced, while conducting deeper assessments of vulnerabilities that could affect transactions or expose customer information.

Credential Theft And Social Engineering Add To Exposure

The potential consequences of a data leak extend beyond the immediate exposure of records. Information such as phone numbers, dates of birth and loan-related details can be used to make fraudulent communications appear credible, increasing the risk of targeted phishing and impersonation attempts.

Govind Rammurthy, chief executive and managing director of eScan, said cybercriminals were increasingly exploiting legitimate credentials rather than relying solely on attacks that attempt to break through an organisation’s security perimeter. “The shift is attackers are moving away from breaking in and pivoting towards logging in,” Rammurthy said, pointing to credential theft, social engineering and fraud involving stolen information.

He said AI-generated phishing messages could be more personalised and convincing, while compromised employee devices and vendor systems could provide routes into larger networks. Once attackers obtain valid credentials, their activities may resemble legitimate access, making suspicious behaviour harder to distinguish from routine operations.

For banks, this raises the importance of monitoring unusual access patterns, restricting permissions and reviewing connections with vendors, loan agents and outsourced service providers. Rammurthy also recommended multi-factor authentication, behavioural monitoring and endpoint protection to limit the damage from compromised devices.

Banking Cyber Risks Extend Beyond Individual Applications

The SBI incident comes amid a broader rise in cyber activity affecting Indian organisations. CERT-In reported 29,44,248 cybersecurity incidents in 2025, up from 20,41,360 in 2024. These figures cover cybersecurity incidents across sectors and should not be interpreted as confirmed banking breaches.

Separately, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, CERT-In, the Computer Security Incident Response Team in Finance and SISA released the second edition of the Digital Threat Report 2025–26 for India's banking, financial services, insurance and payments ecosystem in July 2026. The report examined emerging threats, including AI-enabled attacks, across the sector.

Ismael Valenzuela, vice-president of labs, threat research and intelligence at Arctic Wolf, said banks also needed to assess risks in underlying technology and supporting services rather than limiting reviews to customer-facing platforms. “Knowing that a vulnerability exists is only part of the challenge,” Valenzuela said. He called for continuous exposure assessment, real-time asset visibility, attack-path analysis and the ability to detect and contain suspicious activity quickly.

Valenzuela also said AI could help correlate vulnerabilities, threat intelligence and asset information to identify high-risk attack paths and prioritise remediation. However, he stressed that expert oversight remained essential, particularly when isolating systems could affect payments or customer access. His comments concern broader technology risks and do not establish that a particular software vulnerability or AI-enabled attack was responsible for the SBI incident.

Investigation To Establish Source And Extent

SBI has said its core business operations, financial performance and business continuity have not been materially affected. The bank has activated its cyber incident response and containment protocols and appointed an independent CERT-In-empanelled cybersecurity agency to investigate the suspected exposure. The assessment is intended to establish the authenticity and completeness of the records, identify the potential source and determine the associated risks.

The outcome of the investigation will be important in determining whether the information originated from the bank's own systems, an external service provider or another source. Until those findings are available, the number of records examined on the dark web should not be treated as the number of confirmed affected customers, nor should the suspected exposure be equated with unauthorised access to bank accounts.

For banks, the incident underscores the need to combine application security testing with access controls, continuous monitoring, vendor assessments and incident-response procedures that can identify and contain threats across connected systems.

data.title: Indian Shares End Lower, Post Weekly Losses As Surging Oil Prices Fuel Inflation Concerns
data.description:
Indian equity markets ended lower on Friday, posting their second consecutive weekly decline as surging crude oil prices amid heightened Middle East tensions raised concerns over inflation and corporate earnings.

The benchmark Nifty 50 fell 0.39 per cent to 22,600, while the Sensex declined 0.17 per cent to 73,123.83. For the week, the Nifty and Sensex fell 2.4 per cent and 2.2 per cent, respectively.

Brent crude futures climbed to around $114 a barrel amid concerns over global energy supplies following attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen-based Houthi forces. Higher oil prices have raised concerns for India, which relies heavily on crude imports, as increased input costs could weigh on corporate margins and add to inflationary pressures.

Market sentiment was also affected by strong demand for billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Jio Platforms IPO, which had been subscribed 13.8 times by the close of trading, analysts at SMC Global and Motilal Oswal Financial Services said. The large issue is expected to have absorbed liquidity from the secondary market.

Fifteen of the 16 major sectoral indexes recorded weekly losses. Mid-cap and small-cap stocks underperformed the benchmark indices, falling 5.6 per cent and 7.3 per cent, respectively. Both segments recorded their steepest weekly declines in 20 months.

Consumer durables, energy, FMCG and auto stocks were among the major decliners, falling 6.4 per cent, 4.6 per cent, 4.3 per cent and 3.5 per cent, respectively. Higher crude prices have raised concerns over earnings prospects for sectors exposed to oil and other input costs.

Among individual stocks, HDFC Bank, the heaviest-weighted stock in the benchmark, declined 5 per cent during the week after its quarterly profit fell short of market expectations. Axis Bank lost 5.6 per cent following an earnings miss, while Bajaj Finance dropped 5.4 per cent as concerns over lending margins outweighed an increase in quarterly profit.

On Friday, Swiggy plunged 16.8 per cent to a record low amid concerns over the company's ability to improve the performance of its quick-commerce business and margins in its food-delivery operations.

Colgate-Palmolive India also declined 4.8 per cent after its quarterly profit missed analysts' estimates.

The combination of elevated crude prices, weak global cues, earnings disappointments and liquidity pressure from the primary market weighed on investor sentiment through the week.

data.title: Adani Power Q2 Profit Rises 142% To Rs 7,019 Cr On Higher Revenue
data.description:
Profit growth was supported by higher power sales and a rise in plant load factor, alongside increased recognition of prior-period income

Adani Power reported a 141.5 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 7,019 crore for the September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 2,906 crore in the year-ago period. The increase was supported by stronger operating performance and higher recognition of prior-period income.

Reported revenue rose 39.4 per cent to Rs 19,951 crore from Rs 14,308 crore a year earlier. Reported earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) increased 45.7 per cent to Rs 8,743 crore from Rs 6,001 crore.

Core Operating Performance

Excluding prior-period income recognition, continuing revenue increased 28.5 per cent to Rs 17,528 crore, while continuing EBITDA grew 18.5 per cent to Rs 6,321 crore. The company attributed the growth to higher power sales, improved tariffs and better realisation in merchant markets, despite rising fuel costs.

Adani Power recognised Rs 2,422 crore in prior-period revenue during the quarter, primarily due to revisions in historical energy charges under certain power purchase agreements. This compared with Rs 669 crore recognised in the corresponding quarter last year.

Continuing profit before tax rose 32.5 per cent to Rs 4,370 crore from Rs 3,298 crore a year earlier. Finance costs declined 9.7 per cent to Rs 760 crore, which the company attributed to stronger operating cash flows and controlled utilisation of operational debt.

Power Sales And Expansion

Consolidated power sales increased 11.5 per cent to 26.4 billion units during the quarter, compared with 23.7 billion units a year earlier. The plant load factor, a measure of capacity utilisation, rose to 70.1 per cent from 62.8 per cent.

Power sales under power purchase agreements increased 29.7 per cent to 23.4 billion units, while tariff realisation improved 12.7 per cent to Rs 6.4 per kilowatt-hour. Merchant and short-term market realisation rose 33.1 per cent to Rs 7.2 per kilowatt-hour, although volumes supplied in these markets declined 43 per cent.

The company is progressing with plans to add 23,720 MW of thermal power capacity. The first 660 MW unit of the Korba Phase II project has been synchronised with the grid, with commissioning expected shortly. The second unit is expected to be commissioned in the fourth quarter of FY27.

Separately, Adani Power has received a letter of award from Uttarakhand Power Corporation for a 25-year power supply agreement covering 1,320 MW of thermal power capacity, equivalent to 1,234 MW on a net basis. The agreement will increase power tie-ups for its upcoming thermal capacity to 62 per cent.

data.title: Welspun Corp Secures United States Gas Pipeline Order Worth Rs 5,500 Cr
data.description:
The order was won by its US subsidiary and will be executed from the company’s United States facility during FY29

Welspun Corp has secured an order worth approximately Rs 5,500 crore from a major US midstream company to supply coated line pipes for a natural gas pipeline project in the Permian region of the United States, the company said in an exchange filing on Friday.

The order was won by Welspun Tubular LLC, the company’s US subsidiary, and will be executed from its US manufacturing facility during FY29. Following the order, Welspun Corp’s global order book has reached a record USD 5.25 billion, equivalent to around Rs 50,000 crore.

The pipeline will supply natural gas to an anchor customer that operates a data centre complex and is one of the world’s top-tier hyperscalers, according to the company. Welspun did not disclose the identity of the customer or the capacity of the planned pipeline.

The company said the project connects its pipeline business with the growing requirement for energy transmission infrastructure supporting AI-led data centre expansion. The development comes as large data centre facilities increase their demand for reliable power and related energy infrastructure.

US Orders Boost Backlog

The latest contract follows a series of large order wins by Welspun Corp in the US market. In September, its US subsidiary secured an order worth approximately USD 412.5 million for high-frequency induction welded pipes, which will be manufactured at its upgraded facility in Little Rock, Arkansas.

In August, Welspun Corp had announced an order worth around USD 1.8 billion for pipe supplies from its US manufacturing facility, making it the company’s largest-ever single order. The contract is scheduled for execution during FY28 and FY29, adding to the company’s pipeline of US projects.

With the latest order, Welspun Corp’s global order book has reached its highest-ever level at approximately USD 5.25 billion. The company’s recent US contracts have increased its exposure to pipeline infrastructure demand while expanding its manufacturing order visibility through FY29.

data.title: GP Petroleums Appoints Shirish Suvagia As CFO
data.description:
The appointment brings over 23 years of finance experience as the lubricants company pursues expansion in domestic and international markets

GP Petroleums Limited has appointed Shirish Suvagia as Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Key Managerial Personnel, effective 15 October 2026. A Chartered Accountant with over 23 years of experience, Suvagia brings expertise in corporate finance, treasury, strategic financial planning, mergers and acquisitions, and fundraising as the company looks to strengthen its financial leadership and support business expansion.

In his new role, Suvagia will oversee the company’s finance function, including financial strategy, treasury, business planning, capital allocation, fundraising, risk management, financial reporting and internal controls. The appointment comes as GP Petroleums continues to expand its lubricants business and pursue growth opportunities in India and international markets.

Experience Across Corporate Finance

Suvagia has more than two decades of experience across finance and strategic planning. His professional background includes leading treasury operations, debt and private equity fundraising initiatives, financial transformation projects, and the implementation of Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).

He has also been involved in initial public offering (IPO) and rights issue-related transactions, including the preparation of Draft Red Herring Prospectuses and Draft Letters of Offer. His experience spans capital raising, financial planning and controls, areas relevant to the company’s expansion and capital allocation priorities.

Academic And Professional Credentials

Suvagia holds bachelor’s and master’s degrees in commerce from the University of Mumbai, an Executive MBA in Strategy from IIM Indore, a Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA) certification from ISACA, and an IFRS certification from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI).

His appointment adds experience in treasury management, fundraising and financial planning to GP Petroleums’ leadership team as it focuses on capital efficiency and long-term growth.

Leadership Focus On Growth

Commenting on the appointment, Ayush Goel, Chairman and Managing Director of GP Petroleums, said, “We are delighted to welcome Mr. Suvagia to GP Petroleums. His experience across corporate finance, treasury, fundraising and mergers & acquisitions will be a valuable asset to the Company, particularly as we focus on capital allocation, business expansion and long-term value creation. We look forward to his contribution as we take the company forward. We are confident that his leadership and financial expertise will support the Company in creating sustainable value for all stakeholders.”

Suvagia said, “I am excited to join GP Petroleums at an important stage of its growth journey. IPOL is a well-established and respected brand with strong market fundamentals and significant opportunities ahead. I look forward to partnering with the Board and leadership team to further strengthen the Company's financial capabilities, support strategic growth initiatives, and drive long-term value creation for stakeholders.”

The appointment places Suvagia at the helm of GP Petroleums’ financial operations as the company pursues expansion while focusing on financial discipline, risk management and capital allocation.

data.title: Cognizant To Acquire DyFlex Solutions To Expand SAP & AI Capabilities
data.description:
The deal will strengthen enterprise technology services across Australia and New Zealand, with completion expected in early 2027

Cognizant has signed a definitive agreement to acquire DyFlex Solutions, an Australia-headquartered, AI-led SAP transformation firm, to expand its enterprise technology and artificial intelligence capabilities across Australia and New Zealand. The acquisition is expected to strengthen Cognizant’s SAP and enterprise platform services, helping regional clients modernise core business systems and accelerate digital transformation.

DyFlex is a SAP Platinum Partner with more than 300 employees. It provides advisory, consulting, implementation and managed services, with delivery operations extending to the Philippines. Its expertise is expected to complement Cognizant’s capabilities in artificial intelligence (AI), cloud services and its Autonomous Enterprise strategy.

Expanding Regional Capabilities

The acquisition will broaden Cognizant’s enterprise technology capabilities in Australia and New Zealand, where businesses across several sectors are investing in modernising core systems and digital operations.

By combining DyFlex’s SAP expertise with Cognizant’s broader technology portfolio, the companies aim to support clients in upgrading enterprise platforms and integrating AI-led capabilities into business processes.

Focus On Key Industries

DyFlex serves industries including mining and resources, energy and utilities, manufacturing, logistics and the public sector. These sectors rely on enterprise systems to manage complex operations, supply chains, resources and service delivery.

The acquisition is expected to strengthen Cognizant’s ability to provide SAP-related services across these industries, combining implementation and managed services with cloud and AI capabilities.

Combining SAP And AI

The deal brings together DyFlex’s experience in SAP transformation with Cognizant’s AI, cloud and Autonomous Enterprise capabilities. The combined offering is intended to help organisations modernise core systems and advance their digital transformation programmes.

DyFlex’s advisory and consulting services, alongside its implementation and managed services, will add to Cognizant’s enterprise platform capabilities in the region.

Completion In Early 2027

Cognizant expects the acquisition to be completed in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed in the provided announcement.

The proposed deal represents an expansion of Cognizant’s regional enterprise technology operations, with a focus on SAP services and AI-led transformation for businesses across Australia and New Zealand.

data.title: Tata Consumer Products launches luxury tea collection under 1868 by Tata Tea
data.description:
Tata Consumer Products has launched 1868 by Tata Tea - Crafted for Connoisseurs, a luxury tea collection aimed at consumers seeking distinctive flavours and tea experiences.

Inspired by the year Jamsetji Tata founded the Tata Group, the collection focuses on tea origins, craftsmanship and flavour. It brings together teas from Indian growing regions, blending expertise and selected ingredients.

The inaugural collection features three variants. Masala Chai combines premium-grade tea with real spices, while Cream of Assam uses Assam tea with selected golden tips. Gourmet Street Chai combines handpicked Assam tea with real ginger and cardamom, drawing inspiration from India's chai culture.

Sharat Verma, president, packaged beverages and Organic India, Tata Consumer Products, said, “India has one of the richest tea cultures in the world, but we rarely stop to discover just how extraordinary tea can be. With 1868 by Tata Tea, we want to change that. From distinctive origins and golden-tipped Assam teas to blends crafted with real spices, every tea has been created to offer an experience worth slowing down for. 1868 is our invitation to rediscover something deeply familiar — and experience it in an entirely new way.”

The launch extends Tata Tea's portfolio into the luxury tea segment, with a focus on distinctive blends and curated tea experiences.

data.title: Merck CEO Plays Down Cost Concerns Over Intismeran — ‘We Don't See Cost As A Limit To Access’
data.description:
Key points:
  • On Thursday, MRNA shares plunged more than 17% after Phase 3 trial data was leaked ahead of Saturday’s ESMO presentation.
  • Intismeran, combined with Keytruda, reduced the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 58% after six months, compared with Keytruda alone.
  • Merck and Moderna anticipate potential approval of the drug in 2027.

Merck (MRK) CEO Rob Davis expressed confidence in the commercial potential of the much-talked-about personalised cancer vaccine, Intismeran, playing down concerns that its complex manufacturing process could make the treatment too expensive for patients.

His comments came after Citi questioned whether the vaccine’s clinical benefits justify the cost and complexity of production.

In an interview with CNBC on Friday, Davis credited Moderna’s mRNA technology and specialized manufacturing process for making personalized cancer vaccines commercially viable.

“We think we will have very competitive costs, and we don’t see cost as a limit to access,” Davis said.

At the time of writing, MRK shares were down 2.2% while MRNA stock traded 0.1% lower.

Davis ‘Very Confident’ On Delivering Vaccine On Scale

Intismeran is a personalized cancer vaccine being developed using Moderna’s mRNA technology. The two companies are jointly developing the treatment, which is being tested alongside Merck’s blockbuster cancer drug Keytruda. Unlike traditional vaccines, Intismeran is customized using genetic mutations identified in each patient’s tumor.

Davis said the process currently takes about six weeks, from analyzing a patient’s tumor to manufacturing the vaccine. “So it’s actually very efficient, and one, we feel very confident, we can deliver on scale,” Davis added.

Intismeran, Keytruda Reduced Risk Of Melanoma Recurrence Or Death By 58% After Six Months

On Thursday, MRNA shares plunged more than 17% after Phase 3 trial data, which was leaked ahead of Saturday’s ESMO presentation, fell short of investors’ expectations, triggering what analysts described as a “sell-the-news” reaction.

Merck and Moderna subsequently released the official findings, with Intismeran, combined with Keytruda, reducing the risk of cancer returning or death by 42% compared with Keytruda alone. The results were even better after six months, with the combination reducing the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 58%, compared with Keytruda alone.

“What’s not appreciated is because this is an immunisation, much like you would get if you got a vaccine, you really need to look at the six-month data. That’s the time that allows your body to fully mount an immune response at six months, and it has reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 58%. So this is meaningful if you’re a patient,” Davis said.

Potential Approval in 2027

Davis said Merck and Moderna are moving quickly to seek regulatory approval for Intismeran, with hopes of filing an application before the end of 2026.

"We’re working as fast as we can right now to get the file in,” Davis said, adding that the companies anticipate potential approval sometime in 2027.

Retail’s Take On MRNA, MRK

Retail sentiment surrounding MRK on Stocktwits remained ‘bullish’ over the past 24 hours while sentiment for MRNA turned ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ over the same period.

Chatter largely centered on the data, which left some users disappointed.

While MRK shares have climbed 36% so far this year, MRNA continues to be among the top biotech gainers, with a 550% surge.

data.title: SK Hynix and Samsung likely to boost shareholder returns as demand stays strong: BofA
data.description:
SK Hynix and Samsung have seen their fortunes swell thanks to the boom in the memory market, and Bank of America believes the two South Korean giants could further reward shareholders as a result.

“We see potential catalysts in additional shareholder returns from SK Hynix (a special year-end cash dividend following its recent W40tn buyback) and Samsung Electronics (a new buyback post-3Q cash dividend of W30tn),” Bank of America analysts led by Simon Woo wrote in a note to clients. “Both could address these returns at their respective earnings calls on 28-29 Oct. We expect Korean memory chipmakers to step up dividends and buybacks, given exceptionally low P/E ratios (following severe share- price corrections) and strong growth in FCF (despite concerns about a downturn).”

As of the fourth quarter, the annualized free cash flow for SK Hynix and Samsung has exceeded $150B and $226B, respectively. The analysts believe that SK Hynix will keep its shareholder return splits for buybacks and dividends at 60% and 40%, respectively, and 40% and 60% for Samsung.

SK Hynix is set to report its next quarterly results later this month, and the analysts believe the company will offer up “bullish guidance,” due in part to the successful ramp-up of 12-hi HBM4. There could be additional production of 8-hi HBM4 if Nvidia pays a price premium per bit of around 10%.

Separately, Samsung could see gains in the high-bandwidth memory market and the contract pricing in its long-term agreements offers upside, as deliveries extend out to 2029 and 2030.

data.title: Worthington Steel Confirms Its Kloeckner Strategy Following Shareholder Vote
data.description:
Worthington Steel, Inc. () today announced that the proposed domination and profit and loss transfer agreement (“DPLTA”) between Kloeckner & Co SE (“Kloeckner”) and Worthington Steel GmbH, a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of Worthington Steel, did not receive the required shareholder approval at Kloeckner’s extraordinary general meeting in Düsseldorf, Germany. As a result, the DPLTA will not become effective. Worthington Steel remains committed to delivering on the long-term strategic and economic rationale of the transaction. For now, the company will operate within the existing ownership and governance structure and will pursue commercial, procurement, operational and strategic opportunities that can be advanced within that framework and in accordance with applicable law.

“The path forward is clear, and we will begin work immediately,” said Geoff Gilmore, Worthington Steel President and CEO. “The vote will affect the timing, mix and manner in which certain goals can be realized, particularly in the near term, but it does not change our conviction regarding the compelling strategic rationale for the acquisition. We continue to see significant long-term synergy and value-creation potential and will pursue relevant opportunities consistent with the existing governance framework.”

Worthington Steel has included Kloeckner’s financial results in its consolidated financial reporting since completing the acquisition of a majority stake in June 2026. The outcome of the vote does not affect this financial consolidation or its financing arrangements.

Worthington Steel completed its voluntary public takeover offer for Kloeckner on June 3, 2026. Following the subsequent public delisting tender offer, Worthington Steel currently holds approximately 62% of Kloeckner’s share capital and voting rights. Following the vote, Worthington Steel’s existing majority stake in Kloeckner and its strategic commitment to the combination remain unaffected.

At the extraordinary general meeting, Kloeckner shareholders approved the proposed election of five Supervisory Board members who had already been serving on the Board following their court appointment in July 2026. Shareholders also approved amendments to Kloeckner’s Articles of Association intended to simplify ongoing corporate governance.

Further information on the public takeover offer and public delisting offer is available at www.strong-for-good.com.

About Worthington Steel

Worthington Steel () is one of North America's leading value-added metals processing and manufacturing companies. The Company partners with customers to deliver specialized, highly technical solutions across carbon flat-rolled steel, aluminum, stainless steel, long products, heavy plate and electrical steel, to solve complex challenges across a broad range of industries.

Worthington Steel employs approximately 12,000 people and operates approximately 150 facilities, primarily in North America, with additional operations in Europe and Asia. The Company combines extensive processing expertise with advanced manufacturing technologies, including galvanizing, pickling, configured blanking, specialty cold reduction, electrical steel laminations, fabrication and precision processing.

Guided by its people-first Philosophy and a commitment to safety, innovation and continuous improvement, Worthington Steel creates long-term value by delivering trusted solutions for customers, opportunities for employees, returns for shareholders and strength for the communities where it operates.

Important Information: The employee and facility counts above reflect the combined totals of Worthington’s wholly owned businesses, consolidated affiliates including Kloeckner, and unconsolidated affiliate consistent with our past practices.

About Kloeckner & Co

Kloeckner & Co is one of the largest producer-independent metals processors and one of the leading steel service center companies. With its distribution and service network of around 110 warehouse and processing locations, primarily in North America and the “DACH” region (Germany, Austria and Switzerland), Kloeckner & Co supplies more than 60,000 customers. Currently, the Group has more than 6,000 employees. Kloeckner & Co had sales of some €6.4 billion in fiscal year 2025. By consistently implementing its corporate strategy, Kloeckner & Co strives to become one of the leading service center and metal processing companies in North America and Europe. The focus is on continued targeted expansion of the service center and higher value-added business, diversification of the product and service portfolio as well as integration of additional CO2-reduced solutions under the Nexigen® umbrella brand.

All forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties which could cause actual results to differ from those projected. Factors that could cause actual results to differ materially include, but are not limited to, limitations on Worthington Steel’s ability to direct Kloeckner’s operations under the existing governance framework; delays in or failure to realize anticipated synergies and other acquisition benefits; and risks, uncertainties and impacts described from time to time in Worthington Steel’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

data.title: Wells Fargo, Intuit latest companies to object to their shares being tokenized, document shows
data.description:
Key points:
  • In total, 22 companies have objected to OKXICE stock tokenization, document shows
  • OKX and ICE had planned to tokenize 63 stocks through their joint venture
  • SEC exemption bars platforms from listing tokenized shares if issuer objects

By Hannah Lang

Six more companies, including Wells Fargo , Arm Holdings and Intuit , will not allow their shares to be tokenized on a joint trading platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange , according to a regulatory document seen by Reuters.

The new objections, which have not been previously reported, underscore the growing challenges for tokenization, the creation of digital tokens that represent a stock and can be traded on a blockchain similar to cryptocurrencies, despite the US securities regulator recently approving the novel products.

In total, 22 companies have objected, according to the document, which outlines the rules of the OKXICE venture and which companies have objected. It does not say why the companies objected.

Sixteen of the companies, including Microsoft and Alphabet , are listed on Nasdaq . The others are listed on the New York Stock Exchange, which ICE owns.

Spokespeople for Arm and Intuit did not immediately provide comment. A Wells Fargo spokesperson declined to comment.

TOKENIZATION ADVOCATES TOUT 24/7 TRADING

The cryptocurrency industry has said stock tokenization could revolutionize markets by allowing shares to be traded 24/7 and settled instantly. OKX and ICE had planned to tokenize 63 stocks through their joint venture, dubbed OKXICE, but have encountered objections from issuers.

OKX and ICE filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this month to launch tokenized stocks under the agency's new innovation exemption. The exemption allows platforms that facilitate trading of tokenized stocks to operate without complying with many requirements that apply ​to traditional stock exchanges.

Under the exemption, platforms must notify companies before listing tokenized versions of their stocks, and cannot proceed if the issuer objects.

Speaking to reporters this week, Andrew Cuomo, co-chairman of the OKXICE joint venture, said given how revolutionary tokenization could be, it was natural for companies to take a "wait and see" approach, CoinDesk reported.

While Nasdaq says it welcomes tokenization in principle, it has said such products should be subject to the existing set of rules and investor protections. It has warned that if improperly regulated, tokenization could fragment liquidity and undermine price discovery, among other issues.

"Given the risks we believe issuers must be cautious about their participation," the company warned in a September FAQ.

A Nasdaq spokesperson pointed Reuters to its FAQ.

Although many overseas tokenized stocks are marketed like stocks, they rarely offer the same rights, disclosures and protections as traditional equities.

Under the SEC's exemption, tokenized stocks must confer the same rights and privileges as ​traditional securities, including the ability to receive dividends and exercise voting rights.

data.title: Bombardier to Invest $270 Million in U.S. Expansion as Trump Softens Stance — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

Bombardier plans to invest $270 million to expand its American infrastructure footprint and hire 800 U.S. workers, days after President Trump appeared to soften his rhetoric against the Montreal-based business-jet maker.

The expansion includes a significant step-up in operations in Texas, opening a new service center in Indiana, building a learning hub in Kansas, as well as launching additional infrastructure projects in Connecticut.

In a Truth Social post at 11:41 P.M. Thursday, hours before Bombardier's official announcement, Trump praised Bombardier's plans, stating "Bombardier is investing 270 MILLION DOLLARS, creating THOUSANDS of American Jobs in Kansas, Texas, and Indiana."

Bombardier's expansion will directly add 800 U.S. jobs, 300 by way of new projects and 500 through active recruitment, it said on Friday.

The company estimates it has spent $2.8 billion across its U.S. supply chain in 2025 and expects its new hiring initiative to push total direct and indirect American jobs supported by its operations beyond 33,000, with employment presence across more than 20 states.

The capital push comes a few days after Trump made an apparent reference to the Canadian company at a recent rally.

"I'm going to be helping a certain air company get themselves straightened away," he said to the crowd, after he learned it has significant domestic operations.

Bombardier has repeatedly found itself in the crosshairs during the escalating trade tensions between the Trump administration and Canada.

The latest tensions began after an earlier Trump post on Truth Social last month when he said Bombardier was treating the U.S. like a "piggybank," while taking advantage of U.S. buyers, airports, and infrastructure.

"NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES! Their products aren't good enough!" Trump wrote on Labor Day, urging followers to "Buy American. Fly on American airliners."

Bombardier responded by highlighting its deep U.S. footprint, noting that its jets rely heavily on American-made components such as engines, avionics and other critical aircraft systems. The U.S. is also Bombardier's single largest market for business jets, generating a substantial portion of its overall revenues.

As part of its $270 million U.S. initiative--which includes $50 million dedicated to Kansas--Bombardier recently inaugurated a learning center in Wichita, a new North American hub for learning, developing aerospace talent, enhancing capabilities and supporting the long-term growth of its local operations.

In Fort Wayne, Ind., Bombardier will open its roughly 64,500-square-foot service facility in November, which is expected to accommodate up to six business jets for routine maintenance, avionics installations and emergency repair support.

The company also plans to launch additional footprint-expansion projects in Dallas, Texas and Connecticut.

data.title: SEC To Increase Scrutiny of Advisers Recommending SPV Investments — WSJ
data.description:
By Corrie Driebusch

The Securities and Exchange Commission will prioritize reviewing investment advisers that recommend investments in private companies through special purpose vehicles, it said in its 2027 Examination Priorities on Friday.

It follows SEC examiners asking registered investment advisers for proof that their SPVs own or have exposure to the shares in private companies that they claim to, the Journal has reported. Regulators decided to take a closer look following increased investor complaints and a marketing campaign by such funds ahead of SpaceX's initial public offering in June and Anthropic's planned IPO next month.

In August the Journal reported on an SPV fund that advertised pre-IPO exposure to SpaceX but later told investors the shares were sold before trading in the rocket company began, limiting investors' expected gains.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.description:
RNS Number : 2831A VinaCapital Vietnam Opportunity Fd. 23 October 2026  

VinaCapital Vietnam Opportunity Fund Limited

(the "Company" or "VOF")

LEI Number: 2138007UD8FBBVAX9469

Revaluations of Investments as at 30 June 2026

As part of the review of the Company's Financial Statements for the year ended 30 June 2026, the audit committee of the Company has updated the valuations of unquoted investments held in the Company's portfolio. In some cases these valuations are prepared by VinaCapital Investment Management Limited and, in other cases, by KPMG Tax and Advisory Limited as independent valuers.

Across the portfolio there were some upwards revaluations and some downwards adjustments and, in aggregate, the revised valuations have resulted in a increase of the Company's Net Asset Value (NAV) as at 30 June 2026 of USD 7.4 million - 0.80% of the NAV.  These revised valuations will be included in the calculation of the daily NAV for 23 October 2026 to be issued on 26 October and will be used for the daily NAVs from that point forward until the assets are next revalued.

Full information is included in the Annual Report and Financial Statements of the Company for the year ended 30 June 2026 which are being released on 26 October 2026.

Further information is available on the Company’s website at: https://vof.vinacapital.com/

Dividend Declaration

The Board of Directors of the Company is pleased to announce the declaration of a dividend of 7.25 US cents per share, payable to shareholders on or around 9 December 2026.

Currency of Payment

The dividend will be paid via BACS or by the CREST settlement system or by cheque in Pounds Sterling to shareholders with registered addresses in the UK or Channel Islands and US dollars to shareholders with registered addresses elsewhere.

Shareholders with addresses in the UK or Channel Islands who wish to receive their dividends in US dollars and shareholders elsewhere who wish to receive their dividends in Pounds Sterling may elect to do so by instructing the Company's Registrar, Computershare Investor Services (Guernsey) Ltd, in writing at the address below.

Computershare Investor Services (Guernsey) Limited

C/o 13 Castle Street

St Helier

Jersey

JE1 1ES

Channel Islands

In order to be valid, letters must be received by the Registrar no later than close of business on 16 November 2026.

The exchange rate for determining the dividend amount in Pounds Sterling will be confirmed by way of an announcement by the Company on or around 23 November 2026.

Timetable

The record date for dividends will be 6 November 2026. The shares will trade ex-dividend from 5 November 2026.
